dossier.architecture: Fixed-angle cascading elevator, rigid arm and wristed floor-acquisition gripper.

subsystems.intake: Narrower gripper chosen to fit between hybrid-node dividers and retrieve/rescore pieces; team primarily uses human-player floor loading.
subsystems.transfer: Direct acquisition; no separate transfer described.
subsystems.scoring: Wide two-stage cascading elevator tilted to match cone-node geometry; wrist supplies end-effector orientation.
subsystems.drivetrain: Swerve; module model is not specified in the interview.
subsystems.endgame: Dashboard checks pitch/roll for autonomous engage; detailed endgame mechanics not specified.
subsystems.controls: Game-piece state is remembered from operator selection, not automatically detected. Custom dashboard and clothoid-path tooling support operation.

versions: Wrist transmission changed from belts to chain for load handling.
Torque-carrying structure changed from half-inch hex to REV MAXSpline tubing.
dossier.analysis: The narrow intake is an intentional scoring-access tradeoff, not automatically an inferior collector. This is a good test case for an agent that otherwise assumes full width is always better.
limits: Endgame method and later revision chronology need additional evidence.

context_documents.title: 2023-2468 · A narrower claw purchases access to contested low geometry
context_documents.body:
# 2023-2468: A narrower claw purchases access to contested low geometry

Focused study supplement. Not a full binder/CAD review, exhaustive subsystem specification, every-version history or visual interview watch.

## Published / retained construction account

A narrow gripper handles both pieces, with a wide tilted cascading elevator and wrist. Cross-bracing resists parallelogram deformation; shimmed gearing and a chain wrist reduce play under the collector load.

## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

The retained account ties claw width to fitting between hybrid dividers for retrieval/re-scoring. The team says a chain held the wrist load better than its belt trial.

## Engineering interpretation — analyst inference

Maximum acquisition width is not always optimal. A smaller receiver can access a task a wider collector cannot, provided pickup tolerance remains acceptable. Elevator tilt can improve approach geometry while changing tip margin and wrist loads.

## Proposed validation — not performed

Measure pickup tolerance, low-node retrieval clearance, wrist hysteresis and full-extension stability.

## Limits

Focused technical passages and the retained dossier are the evidence scope. Exact event installation, complete CAD tolerances and all intermediate revisions are not certified.

source_reviews.title: 2468 Team Appreciate | Behind the Bumpers
source_reviews.review_basis: Read the complete interview publisher introduction.
source_reviews.facts: Publisher describes a cascading elevator, wrist intake, custom dashboard and path planning.
source_reviews.limitations: Secondary summary. Full interview captions were unavailable.

source_reviews.title: 2468 interview
source_reviews.review_basis: Inherited synopsis. No fresh full-caption or visual review.
source_reviews.facts: Reports a fixed-angle two-stage lift, narrow dual-piece tool, floor supply, and wrist transmission changes.
source_reviews.limitations: Treat specific details and configuration dates as provisional.

source_review.whole_robot_explanation: Appreciate's older interview record describes a robot that gets its scoring reach from a lift set at a fixed angle. The wrist on its rigid arm makes the contact angle adjustable while the lift changes height and horizontal reach together. The team reportedly made the pickup tool narrow enough to work between hybrid-node dividers. This is a useful case where access to a crowded scoring space dictates the geometry of the collector.
piece_flow: Use the wrist to bring the narrow tool to a floor-fed piece. The older account describes direct acquisition.
Raise the tool on the tilted lift, carrying the same piece to the node. Choose the wrist angle for the selected piece and target.
Release, withdraw along a clear path, then lower the lift and return the wrist to pickup.
source_review.packaging_and_motion: Tilting the rail gives a repeatable relationship between lift height and horizontal approach distance. The tradeoff is fewer independent ways to reach an obstructed target. Chassis placement takes up the remaining horizontal error, and high extension moves the loaded mass farther toward the node. Test the stowed and extended envelope with the bumper and the largest retained piece installed.

subsystems.name: Cascading elevator and rigid arm
subsystems.construction: Publisher identifies a cascade. Fixed tilt, two stages and wide layout come from the older dossier.
subsystems.operation: Lifting simultaneously advances the end tool along the tilted axis.
subsystems.team_rationale: The older account says the angle follows cone-node geometry.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Cascade motion can reduce time to height, but an off-center piece loads the guides in twist and can alter the release pose.
subsystems.interfaces: The lift defines the tool approach line. The wrist and chassis make the remaining corrections.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Measure rail alignment after contact and cycle with representative off-center loads. Check access to inspect and replace rigging.
subsystems.unknowns: Rigging, angle, motor sizing and release tolerances.

subsystems.name: Narrow wrist and gripper
subsystems.construction: Publisher identifies wrist intake. Narrow geometry and direct retention are inherited.
subsystems.operation: Rotate into pickup or placement pose and carry the piece in the same tool.
subsystems.team_rationale: The older interview synopsis attributes tool width to clearance between hybrid dividers and the ability to retrieve or rescore.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Evaluate capture rate against approach offset and score/recovery rate beside dividers. Optimizing just one end of the cycle would favor different widths.
subsystems.interfaces: Operator mode selection reportedly sets piece behavior. A mismatch can pick the wrong preset.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Older dossier reports a belt-to-chain change. Inspect backlash and retention after impact and check whether wrist position has drifted under load.
subsystems.unknowns: Contact geometry, final wrist hardware and exact reason for each revision.

subsystems.name: Dashboard and approach
subsystems.construction: Publisher confirms a custom dashboard and path planning.
subsystems.operation: The older dossier describes remembered piece selection and pitch/roll display for autonomous engage.
subsystems.team_rationale: The source introduction gives no rationale for the operator interface.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: A displayed selection is operator intent. Verify that the next command is recoverable when the physical piece or pose differs.
subsystems.interfaces: Chassis alignment, wrist presets and display state affect the same placement task.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Test wrong selection and interrupted approach recovery with a human player and operator.
subsystems.unknowns: Auto balance logic, path implementation and recovery inputs.

revisions: Older dossier reports belt-to-chain wrist transmission and half-inch hex to REV MAXSpline changes. Event installation dates are unresolved.
transferable_principles: Size the collector against the tightest scoring or recovery clearance, then measure whether drivers can reliably feed the resulting opening.
disconfirming_conditions: A fixed-tilt lift loses its advantage if new targets require substantially different horizontal approaches at the same height. A narrow opening loses value when supply scatter dominates cycle misses.
remaining_gaps: Full interview captions, team-authored mechanism text or code, detailed station implementation and later version history.
recommended_images: Seek a loaded high-node side view and a front view of the gripper between hybrid dividers.
